name: Wing

status.note: Still a pre-1.0 “pre-release”; Wing Cloud, the company behind it, shut down in April 2025, and the project is now community-maintained.

summary: A programming language for the cloud that puts infrastructure and the code that runs on it in one program: the compiler turns it into Terraform for AWS, Azure or Google Cloud plus JavaScript for the functions, and can also run it all in a local simulator.
intro: A Wing program has two phases. Preflight code, the default, runs once at compile time and declares resources: `new cloud.Bucket()`, `new cloud.Queue()`, `new cloud.Api()`. Inflight code, written in blocks marked `inflight`, runs later on cloud compute and uses those resources through their inflight methods, such as `bucket.put()` or `counter.inc()`. The compiler checks that inflight code only calls methods that exist at runtime, and from what each handler touches it generates least-privilege IAM policies and the environment variables that wire them together.

`wing compile` takes a platform. `sim`, the default, runs the whole app in a local cloud simulator, which `wing test` and the Wing Console (a local UI for logs, resources and tests) use. `tf-aws`, `tf-azure` and `tf-gcp` produce Terraform configuration plus JavaScript bundles; on AWS a bucket becomes S3, a queue SQS, a counter a DynamoDB table and a handler a Lambda function. Custom platforms, written in JavaScript, can change how resources are generated, and Wing code can call JavaScript and npm libraries.

Wing was built by Wing Cloud (first called Monada), founded by Elad Ben-Israel, who had worked on the AWS CDK, and Shai Ber. The company shut down in April 2025, and Wing’s site now calls it a community-maintained open source project. After 18 months without a release, Ben-Israel pushed a burst of fixes in August to October 2026, with versions 0.85.50 and 0.85.51 on npm and the Console no longer requiring a sign-in.
strengths: Infrastructure and handler code live in one typed program, so a handler can’t call a resource that isn’t wired to it
The compiler writes IAM policies and resource wiring from what the code uses, instead of you writing them
A local simulator runs the whole app, including queues and buckets, for fast tests without deploying
Output is plain Terraform, so deployment, state and plans work like any other Terraform project
limits: No company behind it since April 2025: development depends on a handful of volunteers, and releases paused for 18 months
Still pre-1.0, with known rough edges, and its own language to learn instead of TypeScript or Python
Built-in platforms target AWS, Azure and Google Cloud through Terraform; the high-level `cloud` resources cover common services, not every cloud feature
A small ecosystem and community compared with Terraform, Pulumi or the AWS CDK

story: Elad Ben-Israel had worked on the AWS CDK at Amazon. In 2022 he and Shai Ber started Monada, later renamed Wing Cloud, to build a language where the cloud is the computer: the GitHub repository was created in June 2022, and the first `winglang` package went to npm in January 2023. The team argued that a library couldn’t express objects whose methods may only be called at runtime, so they built a language with preflight and inflight phases.

In July 2023 Wing Cloud came out of stealth with a $20 million seed round led by Battery Ventures, Grove Ventures and StageOne Ventures, with angels including HashiCorp co-founder Armon Dadgar. It planned to keep the language free and charge for production features of the Wing Console. The project drew more than 100 contributors.

In April 2025 Ben-Israel announced that the company was shutting down, saying developer experience is often not seen as business-critical, which made it hard to build a business on. The last release from the company was 0.85.49 in February 2025. Wing stayed online as an MIT-licensed community project, and in late summer 2026 Ben-Israel returned with dozens of fixes and two new releases.

choices.choice: A new language, not a library
choices.why: The team argued existing languages can’t mark a method as callable only at runtime or stop handlers from capturing mutable compile-time objects, so preflight and inflight are built into the type system.
Instead of a deployment engine of its own, Wing emits Terraform (and, through custom platforms, other formats), leaving state and apply to tools teams already run.

choices.choice: A local simulator as the default target
choices.why: Deploying to test every change is slow, so `sim` runs queues, buckets and functions locally, letting tests cover the whole architecture.

choices.choice: Cloud-portable resources in the standard library
choices.why: `cloud.Bucket` or `cloud.Queue` describe intent, and each platform maps them to a provider’s service, such as S3 and SQS on AWS.

timeline.text: Repository created in June by the team at Monada
First npm release in January; Wing Cloud raises a $20M seed round in July
Last company release, 0.85.49, in February; Wing Cloud shuts down in April
Releases resume with 0.85.50 and 0.85.51 in August, as a community project
